links.comparator_used: Baseline 3D CNN without bias mitigation (and adversarial CF-Net compared against GLM-residualization PMDN)
links.outcome: Age-related bias, balanced accuracy, and calibration (Brier) in Alzheimer's classification from MRI
links.effect: PMDN: balanced accuracy 0.71, Brier ≈ 0.22, near-zero age prediction correlation, with substantially reduced variability vs baseline and CF-Net; CF-Net showed only partial and unstable debiasing
links.tradeoff: CF-Net's debiasing was partial and unstable. No cost or latency burden reported.
links.quote: PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing.

links.comparator_used: Uncalibrated model probabilities (also compared logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning calibration methods against each other)
links.effect: Post hoc calibration improved probability reliability; isotonic regression and Bayesian binning gave the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24)
links.quote: Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24).

design_hint: post hoc calibration and bias mitigation
